source_verification.title: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta
Aberrant binding of mutant HSP47 affects posttranslational modification of type I collagen and leads to osteogenesis imperfecta

second_answer_attack.resolution: Prolyl hydroxylation is an ER collagen-modification step, but SERPINH1 does not encode a prolyl hydroxylase. It encodes HSP47, the collagen-specific ER chaperone that binds and stabilizes procollagen triple helices and participates in collagen quality control and trafficking.

blind_audit.rationale: HSP47 is a collagen-specific molecular chaperone in the endoplasmic reticulum. SERPINH1 deficiency compromises stabilization and quality control of the procollagen triple helix, alters ER-to-Golgi handling, and yields structurally abnormal collagen despite intact COL1A1/COL1A2 coding sequences. Strongest alternative resolved: Prolyl hydroxylation is an ER collagen-modification step, but SERPINH1 does not encode a prolyl hydroxylase. It encodes HSP47, the collagen-specific ER chaperone that binds and stabilizes procollagen triple helices and participates in collagen quality control and trafficking.
